# Development Guide

*Generated by the BMad document-project workflow — deep scan, 2026-07-17.*

Monorepo-wide guide covering `apps/web` (Next.js cockpit), `apps/desktop` (Electron shell), `packages/core` (`@telar/core`, the loom engine), and repo tooling under `scripts/`. See [../README.md](../README.md) for the project's domain model (loom lifecycle: scope → orchestrate → build → verify → (repair) → ready → human accept → done).

## Prerequisites

- **Bun only.** The repo has no npm/yarn/pnpm lockfile — `bun.lock` (lockfileVersion 1) is the single lockfile for the whole workspace tree and is a protected file (never hand-edit; only modify via `bun install`/`bun add`). Install Bun: `curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash`.
- **No Node version pin.** No `"engines"` field exists in the root, `apps/web`, `apps/desktop`, or `packages/core` `package.json`, and there is no `.nvmrc`/`.node-version`/`.bun-version` file. Whatever Node ships bundled with your Bun install is what runs.
- **Runtime binaries Telar itself expects on PATH** (this is not a build requirement — it's what the cockpit's own machine-readiness "Doctor" probes via `execFile(bin, ["--version"])`; see [../apps/web/lib/server/doctor.ts](../apps/web/lib/server/doctor.ts), `BINARIES` const):

  | Binary | Purpose | Install |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `bun` | package manager / test runner / dev server | `curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install \| bash` |
  | `git` | worktree lanes, desktop build snapshots | `xcode-select --install` or `brew install git` |
  | `gh` | GitHub CLI — branch/PR operations for looms | `brew install gh` |
  | `claude` | Claude Code CLI — one of the two agent drivers | `npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` |
  | `codex` | Codex CLI — the other agent driver | `npm i -g @openai/codex` |

- **A logged-in Claude account** for any loom that actually calls a model (dev server boots fine without one; agent runs will fail auth). See [Environment Configuration](#environment-configuration) below.
- **Playwright Chromium**, only if you'll drive the loom Verifier's Critic Panel locally: `bunx playwright install chromium`. The doctor checks for a `chromium-*` dir under `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright`.
- macOS is the only platform exercised by the repo's own tooling — `scripts/build-desktop.sh` and `electron-builder` config in [../apps/desktop/package.json](../apps/desktop/package.json) target `mac`/`arm64` only.

## Installation & Setup

```bash
git clone <repo-url> telar
cd telar
bun install          # installs the whole workspace (apps/*, packages/*)
```

Root `package.json` declares `"workspaces": ["apps/*", "packages/*"]` and has **no `scripts` block at all** — there is no root-level `bun run <x>`; every command is run from inside a workspace directory (`apps/web`, `apps/desktop`, `packages/core`) or as a direct `bun run scripts/<file>.ts` invocation.

`apps/web/package.json` carries Bun-specific trust entries (`"ignoreScripts"`/`"trustedDependencies"` for `sharp` and `unrs-resolver`); `apps/desktop/package.json` trusts `electron`'s postinstall the same way. These are consulted automatically by `bun install` — no action needed.

## Environment Configuration

### `TELAR_HOME`

`TELAR_HOME` relocates Telar's entire state root (project registry, loom working dirs, provider accounts, credentials). Resolved by `telarDir()` in [../packages/core/src/manifest.ts](../packages/core/src/manifest.ts):

```ts
process.env.TELAR_HOME ?? path.join(os.homedir(), ".telar")
```

| Context | Effective home | Set by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/web` dev server | `~/.telar-dev` (unless you already export `TELAR_HOME`) | the `dev` script itself: `TELAR_HOME="${TELAR_HOME:-$HOME/.telar-dev}" next dev` |
| Anything else (prod build, `scripts/telar`, a manual `bun run start`) | `~/.telar` | default in `telarDir()` |
| `scripts/e2e/greenfield-next` | a throwaway tmp dir per run | the harness itself, see [Testing](#testing) |

The dev script defaulting to `~/.telar-dev` is deliberate isolation: day-to-day `apps/web` development never touches your real `~/.telar` registry. The cockpit's Doctor page (`runDoctor()` → `telarHomeCheck()`) surfaces a `warn` whenever the active dir ends in `.telar-dev`, with the remedy text "Running against the dev sandbox — unset TELAR_HOME to target the real ~/.telar." — this is informational, not a failure.

To point the dev server at your real registry: `TELAR_HOME=$HOME/.telar bun run dev` (from `apps/web`).

### Agent provider credentials

There is no single `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`-style env var Telar requires globally. Auth is a per-account, multi-provider system in `packages/core/src`:

- **Provider descriptors** — [../packages/core/src/providers.ts](../packages/core/src/providers.ts), `PROVIDERS` map:

  | Provider | Config-dir env | Token env by auth mode | Login command |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `claude` | `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | `oauth-token` → `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (from `claude setup-token`), `api-key` → `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `claude auth login` |
  | `codex` | `CODEX_HOME` | `api-key` → `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `codex login` |

- **Account registry** — `~/.telar/accounts.json` ([../packages/core/src/accounts.ts](../packages/core/src/accounts.ts)). Seeded on first read (`seed()`) with:
  - `personal` — `provider: "claude"`, `authMode: "subscription"`, **no `configDir`** (deliberate: an explicit `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, even set to `~/.claude`, hashes to a different, empty macOS Keychain entry and 401s; only an unset var resolves the base/system Claude Code login).
  - `work` — auto-added if `~/.claude-work` exists on disk, `configDir: "~/.claude-work"`.
  - `codex` — auto-added if `~/.codex` exists on disk, `configDir: "~/.codex"`.
- **Secrets** — `~/.telar/credentials.json` ([../packages/core/src/secrets.ts](../packages/core/src/secrets.ts)), one token per account name, written with `mode: 0o600` and re-chmod'd on every write. Kept deliberately separate from `accounts.json` (which is safe to read/share) so that file never carries a secret.
- **Subprocess env construction** — `accountEnv(account)` in [../packages/core/src/engine.ts](../packages/core/src/engine.ts) (~line 107): sets the provider's `configDirEnv` from `account.configDir`, or **actively deletes** it when the account has no `configDir` — not merely skips setting it — because an ambient `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` inherited from the parent server process would otherwise silently leak the wrong login onto a `personal` run (the code's own comment calls this "the personal silently resolves to work bug"). For non-subscription auth modes it injects the mode's token env var, preferring an explicitly-named `account.tokenEnv` (hosting path — secret never touches disk) over the local `readSecret()` fallback.
- **Account health** — `accountHealth()` (accounts.ts) is a pure, read-only, content-blind classifier: it checks only for the *existence* of `.credentials.json` (Claude) / `auth.json` (Codex) inside the configDir, never reads contents. A base/Keychain-only login (`personal`) reports `"unknown"` — "can't be verified from disk" — by design, never faked green.

**Practical setup**: log in with whichever CLI you use ordinarily (`claude auth login` for the base `personal` account, or point `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`/`CODEX_HOME` at an existing profile for `work`/`codex`) — Telar does not run its own OAuth flow; the cockpit's Accounts tab and Doctor page just report on and select among logins that already exist on the machine.

### Desktop build env vars

`apps/desktop/build-web.sh` sets `NEXT_OUTPUT=standalone NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-desktop` when invoking `next build`, so the desktop's standalone output tree never collides with the dev server's own `.next`.

### `.env` files

`.gitignore` excludes `.env*` (with `!.env.example` un-ignored), but **no `.env.example` file exists in the repo** — None found. Telar's own config/auth consumption in `apps/web`, `apps/desktop`, and `packages/core` is entirely `process.env.<VAR>` (the vars documented above); none of those apps reads a `.env` file directly. The one exception is `packages/core/src/requirements.ts`'s `readEnvExampleNames(root)`, which does a read-only `fs.readFileSync` of a **target loom project's** `.env.example`/`.env.sample`/`.env.template` (dotenv-style parsing via `parseEnvNames`) during requirements detection — this inspects the project a loom is orchestrating, not Telar's own configuration, but it is a real dotenv-style file read within `packages/core`.

## Running the Apps

### apps/web (cockpit)

```bash
cd apps/web
bun install          # if not already done at root
bun run dev           # next dev, TELAR_HOME defaults to ~/.telar-dev
```

Other scripts ([../apps/web/package.json](../apps/web/package.json)):

```bash
bun run build         # next build (standard Next output, not the desktop standalone build)
bun run start          # next start — serves the build from `bun run build`
bun run lint            # eslint (flat config, no args needed)
```

Note the [../apps/web/AGENTS.md](../apps/web/AGENTS.md) warning (also linked from `apps/web/CLAUDE.md` via `@AGENTS.md`): this is Next.js `16.3.0-canary` with breaking API changes vs. most training data — consult `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing Next-specific code.

### apps/desktop (Electron shell)

Desktop has no dev-mode hot-reload workflow of its own — it boots the **already-built** standalone Next server. From [../apps/desktop/package.json](../apps/desktop/package.json):

```bash
cd apps/desktop
bun run build:web      # bash ./build-web.sh — builds the standalone Next server into apps/web/.next-desktop
bun run smoke            # electron . --smoke — headless smoke check, exits after printing SMOKE_OK
bun run pack              # electron-builder --dir — packages release/mac-arm64/Telar.app
bun run install:app        # bash ./install-app.sh — smoke-tests the packed app, then installs to /Applications/Telar.app and apps/desktop/release/from-origin/Telar.app
```

`build-web.sh` does more than a plain `next build`: it also hand-copies `static`/`public` into the standalone tree (Next's standalone output omits them), materializes a self-contained `@playwright/mcp` closure next to the standalone tree (a devDependency Next's tracing drops, needed at runtime for the packaged Verifier's Critic Panel), and materializes the `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-<os>-<arch>` native CLI binary (~226MB, loaded via `createRequire` at runtime, so static tracing also drops it) into the exact `node_modules` slot the SDK resolves. See [../apps/desktop/build-web.sh](../apps/desktop/build-web.sh) for the full commented pipeline.

For a **repeatable, from-scratch, origin-only build** (never from your dirty working tree), use `scripts/build-desktop.sh` instead — see [Repo Tooling & Scripts](#repo-tooling--scripts).

### packages/core (`@telar/core`)

Not runnable on its own — it is a pure library (`"type": "module"`, `"exports": { ".": "./src/index.ts" }`, no build step, no `scripts` field in [../packages/core/package.json](../packages/core/package.json)). `apps/web` consumes it via `"@telar/core": "workspace:*"`. It is exercised in two ways:

```bash
cd packages/core
bun test                # runs all 98 spec files under packages/core/test/
bunx tsc --noEmit        # typecheck only (typescript is a devDependency; no tsconfig-specific script)
```

There is no way to "run" core in isolation beyond its test suite and typechecking — its executor/weaver/verifier surfaces are driven at runtime by `apps/web`'s API routes.

## Testing

Bun's built-in test runner (`bun test`, auto-discovers `*.test.ts`/`*.spec.ts` recursively, no config file required) is the **only** test tooling used across the repo. There is no root-level `test` script — run `bun test` from the repo root (respects `bunfig.toml`, below) or from inside a specific workspace.

| Part | Test count | Location | Command |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/core` | 98 spec files | `packages/core/test/` | `bun test` (from repo root or `packages/core`) |
| `apps/web` | 9 spec files | `apps/web/lib/` (colocated, e.g. `commands.test.ts`, `transcript.test.ts`, `permissions.test.ts`) | `bun test` |
| `apps/desktop` | 0 real spec files | — | — |

Core's suite spans `accept-commit.test.ts`, `accept-ready.test.ts`, `auto-repair.test.ts`, `bundle.test.ts`, `contract.test.ts`, `critic.test.ts`, `engine-events.test.ts`, `gates.test.ts`, `manifest.test.ts`, `mcp-oauth.test.ts`, `orchestrator.test.ts`, `panel.test.ts`, `verifier-bin.test.ts`, `verify-loom.test.ts`, `weave.test.ts`, `worktree-lifecycle.test.ts`, plus a milestone-numbered `m5-*`/`m9-*`/`m10-*`/`m11-*` series (lane/dispatch/liveness/reconcile/verify-strategy). Web's real specs: `commands.test.ts`, `gallery-fixtures/fixtures.validate.test.ts`, `loom-mcp.answer-blocked.test.ts`, `loom-mcp.remint.test.ts`, `m11-discuss-first-turn.test.ts`, `permissions.test.ts`, `titles.test.ts`, `transcript.test.ts`, `ultra-mcp.test.ts`.

### `bunfig.toml`

Root [../bunfig.toml](../bunfig.toml) exists for exactly one reason — filtering stale build-output test copies out of `bun test`'s recursive discovery:

```toml
[test]
pathIgnorePatterns = ["**/release/**", "**/.next-desktop/**"]
```

Build outputs (`apps/desktop/release/` from electron-builder, `apps/web/.next-desktop/` from the Next standalone trace) both copy web source — including `*.test.ts` files — into packaged bundles; without this filter `bun test` from the repo root would also execute those stale duplicated copies.

### Playwright

`@playwright/test` and `@playwright/mcp` are devDependencies of `apps/web`, but **there is no `playwright.config.*` anywhere in the repo and no human-authored `*.spec.ts` Playwright test files exist.** Playwright here is infrastructure for the agent-driven loom Verifier, not a developer-run e2e suite:

- [../packages/core/src/verifier.ts](../packages/core/src/verifier.ts) resolves the `@playwright/mcp` CLI binary (`resolvePlaywrightMcpBin`) so the Verifier's Critic Panel can drive a real Chromium and take snapshots.
- [../apps/web/lib/server/doctor.ts](../apps/web/lib/server/doctor.ts) `playwrightCheck()` just checks for an installed Chromium cache dir.

If you need Chromium installed for a local Verifier run: `bunx playwright install chromium`.

### scripts/e2e/greenfield-next

A self-contained, isolated end-to-end harness that drives a **real** orchestrated loom end to end (not a mock): scaffolds a minimal Next.js app from an empty directory, weaves → builds → verifies against a real Verification Contract (deterministic gates + a live critic panel) → reaches `ready`, then tears down.

```bash
# static-only check, no live loom, no network, no model calls
bun run scripts/e2e/greenfield-next/sanity.ts        # prints: SANITY OK
bunx tsc --noEmit -p scripts/e2e/greenfield-next/tsconfig.json

# full live run — requires network + a working `personal` Claude account
bun run scripts/e2e/greenfield-next/orchestrate.ts
bun run scripts/e2e/greenfield-next/orchestrate.ts --keep   # leave the run up; Ctrl-C tears down
bun run scripts/e2e/greenfield-next/orchestrate.ts --ui     # also open a throwaway cockpit (only works if your main :3131 dev server is stopped)

# tear down a kept/crashed run
bun run scripts/e2e/greenfield-next/teardown.ts --run <runDir>
```

Isolation: its own `TELAR_HOME` under `os.tmpdir()/telar-e2e-greenfield-next/<runId>`, unique project name and port per run (`runId = wt_<base36 epoch>_<3-byte hex>`). Teardown is one scoped `fs.rm` (guarded by `assertScopedRunDir`, which refuses any dir that isn't a `wt_*` scratch dir) plus one port-scoped kill — it never touches the shared `~/.telar` tree, other registered projects, port 3131, or the repo working tree.

| Env var | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TELAR_E2E_ACCOUNT` | `personal` | account used for live model calls |
| `TELAR_E2E_MAX_TURNS` | `400` | per-build turn ceiling |
| `TELAR_E2E_TIMEOUT_MS` | `1800000` (30 min) | watch timeout |
| `TELAR_E2E_SELF_SERVE` | off | reserved/unused |

This harness is **not wired into any CI** — see [CI/CD](#cicd-none-found) below.

### CI/CD: None found

No `.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.circleci/`, or `Jenkinsfile` exists anywhere in the repo. `bun test`, `eslint`, and the e2e harness are all run manually, or via Telar's own self-dogfooded loom verification (see [`telar.yaml`](#telaryaml-self-manifest) below) — never automatically on push/PR.

## Linting & Conventions

- **ESLint** — [../apps/web/eslint.config.mjs](../apps/web/eslint.config.mjs), the only lint config in the repo. Flat config (`defineConfig` from `eslint/config`) extending `eslint-config-next/core-web-vitals` and `eslint-config-next/typescript`, with a `globalIgnores` override restoring `eslint-config-next`'s own default ignores (`.next/**`, `out/**`, `build/**`, `next-env.d.ts`) since a custom `ignores` block replaces rather than merges with the preset's. Run: `cd apps/web && bun run lint`.
- **No ESLint config in `packages/core` or `apps/desktop`**, and no root-level config — None found.
- **No Prettier, no Biome** — no `.prettierrc*`, no `biome.json*`, no corresponding devDependency anywhere in the repo. None found; formatting is not automated.
- **TypeScript**: `packages/core` uses TypeScript `^6.0.3` with `@types/node@^26.1.0` (its own devDependencies); `apps/web` uses `typescript@^5` with `@types/node@^20`/`@types/react@^19`. These are intentionally different major versions per workspace — do not assume a single repo-wide TS version.
- **Conventions observed in code, not enforced by tooling**: extensive header comments on non-obvious files explaining *why* (see `providers.ts`, `accounts.ts`, `engine.ts`'s `accountEnv`, `secrets.ts`, `manifest.ts`'s `telarDir`) — follow this pattern when adding comparably non-obvious logic (auth/security-sensitive code, atomic-write idioms, isolation guarantees). Atomic file writes follow a consistent `write to .tmp → fs.renameSync` idiom across `accounts.ts`, `secrets.ts`, and `manifest.ts`'s exported `atomicWrite`.

## Common Tasks

**Add a dependency to a workspace:**
```bash
cd apps/web && bun add <pkg>          # or apps/desktop, packages/core
```
Never hand-edit `bun.lock`, `package-lock.json`, or `yarn.lock` (there is only `bun.lock` in this repo; it is a protected file per house convention).

**Run a single test file:**
```bash
bun test packages/core/test/contract.test.ts
bun test apps/web/lib/transcript.test.ts
```

**Typecheck without building:**
```bash
cd packages/core && bunx tsc --noEmit
cd apps/web && bunx tsc --noEmit
```

**Point the dev cockpit at your real (non-sandbox) `~/.telar`:**
```bash
cd apps/web && TELAR_HOME=$HOME/.telar bun run dev
```

**Check machine readiness** (binaries on PATH, GitHub auth, provider account liveness, Playwright Chromium, active `TELAR_HOME`) — open the running cockpit's Doctor view, backed by [../apps/web/lib/server/doctor.ts](../apps/web/lib/server/doctor.ts) `runDoctor()`. It never runs a real login flow, never reads credential file contents, and never surfaces a token.

**Add/inspect a provider account** — via the cockpit's Accounts tab, or directly by editing `~/.telar/accounts.json` (safe to hand-inspect; holds no secrets) through `packages/core`'s `upsertAccount`/`removeAccount`/`setDefaultAccount` exports in [../packages/core/src/accounts.ts](../packages/core/src/accounts.ts) — do not hand-edit `~/.telar/credentials.json` (chmod 0600, holds tokens).

**Build and install a desktop `.app` from your current commit on origin:**
```bash
bash scripts/build-desktop.sh --ref origin/main --out apps/desktop/release/from-origin
```
(See [Repo Tooling & Scripts](#repo-tooling--scripts) for what this actually does.)

## Repo Tooling & Scripts

### scripts/telar — stable cockpit launcher

Executable Bun script ([../scripts/telar](../scripts/telar), shebang `#!/usr/bin/env bun`). This is **not** `apps/web`'s dev server — it's a separate launcher for a **built, stable** Telar checkout (default app dir `~/Projects/personal/telar-stable`, default port `3100`), meant for running a stable copy detached from your active dev checkout. State lives under `~/.telar/launcher/` (`config.json`, `cockpit.pid`, `cockpit.log`, `built-commit`).

```bash
scripts/telar              # = `telar open`: start if needed (rebuild if HEAD changed since last build), then open the browser
scripts/telar open           # same as above, explicit
scripts/telar stop            # SIGTERM the process group; escalates to SIGKILL after a 10s grace period
scripts/telar restart          # stop, then start, then open
scripts/telar status            # prints app dir, current commit, build freshness (current/stale/none), running state
scripts/telar update             # git pull --ff-only && bun install; rebuilds if stale; restarts if it was running
scripts/telar logs                # last 40 log lines
scripts/telar logs -f               # tail -f — the one subcommand that intentionally lingers
```

Idempotent by design: a second `telar open` on an already-running instance just re-opens the browser.

### scripts/build-desktop.sh — pristine origin-only desktop build

Full pipeline ([../scripts/build-desktop.sh](../scripts/build-desktop.sh), bash, `set -euo pipefail`) — builds the desktop `.app` from a **pristine snapshot of an origin git ref**, deliberately never from the working tree, so uncommitted local changes can never ship:

```bash
bash scripts/build-desktop.sh                                    # --ref origin/main --out apps/desktop/release/from-origin (defaults)
bash scripts/build-desktop.sh --ref origin/some-branch --out ./out-dir
```

1. `git fetch --prune origin`, resolves `<ref>^{commit}`, refuses to proceed unless the SHA is reachable from some `origin/*` branch.
2. Creates a throwaway `git worktree add --detach` snapshot in a temp dir (cleaned up via `trap cleanup EXIT`); the live checkout and its `bun.lock` are never touched.
3. `NODE_OPTIONS= bun install --frozen-lockfile` inside the snapshot (uses the snapshot's own committed `bun.lock`).
4. Runs `apps/desktop/build-web.sh` inside the snapshot.
5. Stamps `build-info.json` (`{ shortSha, sha, ref, commitDate, builtAt }`) into the standalone output before packaging.
6. `bunx electron-builder --dir`, asserts `release/mac-arm64/Telar.app` exists.
7. Atomic swap into `--out`: stage → back up any existing dest → `mv` (atomic rename) → remove backup.
8. Smoke test: runs `Telar.app/Contents/MacOS/Telar --smoke`, fails the whole build unless the output contains the literal line `SMOKE_OK`.

### apps/desktop/install-app.sh

Installs an already-packed `.app` (`release/mac-arm64/Telar.app`, produced by `bun run pack`) — smoke-tests it first (fails closed on smoke failure), then atomically refreshes both `/Applications/Telar.app` and `apps/desktop/release/from-origin/Telar.app` via the same `ditto` + `mv` swap idiom.

### scripts/backfill-tool-detail.ts — one-off data migration

Not a test; a one-off, idempotent data-migration script (`#!/usr/bin/env bun`, [../scripts/backfill-tool-detail.ts](../scripts/backfill-tool-detail.ts)):

```bash
bun scripts/backfill-tool-detail.ts --dry-run    # report only, zero writes
bun scripts/backfill-tool-detail.ts                # writes backups + patches ~/.telar/chats.json
```

Recovers `{id, input, output, isError}` on legacy chat "tool" parts that older versions persisted as `{type:"tool", name}` only (before commit `9b71548` started persisting full detail every turn). Replays each affected chat's SDK session transcript (`<configDir>/projects/<cwd-slug>/<sessionId>.jsonl`) and matches legacy tool parts to `tool_use`/`tool_result` blocks **by position/order**, skipping `isSidechain`/`parentToolUseId` sub-agent relay blocks (mirroring `app/api/chat/route.ts`'s own top-level filtering). Safety: only touches parts missing `id`; writes a full pre-image backup of every modified chat to `~/.telar/backfill-backup-<chatId>.json` before any write; skips a chat entirely (never partially patches) if its legacy tool-part count/names don't line up 1:1 with the transcript.

### telar.yaml — self-dogfooding manifest

Root [../telar.yaml](../telar.yaml) is Telar's own project manifest — proof the tool is dogfooded on itself:

```yaml
name: telar
root: /Users/facundo/Projects/personal/telar
adapter: plain
account: personal
baseBranch: main
gates:
  - name: test
    run: bun test
guardrails:
  disallowedTools: []
  protectedPaths: []
```

`adapter: plain` (no framework-specific adapter), `account: personal` (uses the ambient/base Claude login), one verification gate named `test` running bare `bun test` (which — per `bunfig.toml`'s ignore patterns — recursively covers the whole workspace except build-output copies). Both `guardrails` arrays are empty: no disallowed tools, no protected paths configured for loom runs against this repo. (This is a Telar guardrail, unrelated to any Claude Code harness-level protected-files setting a developer's own tooling might separately enforce.)
